models_evaluated: three open-weight large language models (not named in abstract)

links.outcome: Differences in ED-related response safety when user race, gender, and BMI were varied
links.effect: Responses differed significantly by race, gender, and BMI, with body size producing the largest disparities; consistent with a stereotype that EDs affect thin, White women.
links.quote: Responses also differ significantly by race, gender, and BMI, with body size producing the largest disparities.

links.outcome: Whether models recognize implicit ED vulnerability and respond safely without explicit user information
links.effect: High-risk responses were about twice as frequent without bios; explicit ED vulnerability signals improved safety by 10-14 points across models.
links.quote: High-risk responses are approximately twice as frequent without bios, suggesting that models do not consistently recognize vulnerability from language alone.

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of LLM safety and bias when responding to eating disorder queries sourced from an online pro-anorexia forum, examining differences based on user demographic bios.
